prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a retail-like indoor room with glass doors at the back (~3–4 m away), a clothing rack with hanging garments in the right-center foreground (~1–2 m away), a dark hooded figure or mannequin standing by the doors (~2.5–3 m away, ~1–1.5 m behind the rack), and a person in a white shirt and grey jacket on the left (~0.5–1 m away, within arm's reach of the camera wearer). In frame 1, the person on the left is largely cropped out at the edge (~0.5 m away) and occludes the left doorway, while in frame 5, after the camera wearer pitches up toward the ceiling window (frame 3) and turns rapidly across the clothing rack (frame 4), that person stands directly in front of the left side of the frame (~0.8 m away) facing toward the camera wearer with a raised foreground hand/arm (~0.3–0.5 m away, well within arm's reach) partially occluding their chest. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer turns right and tilts upward in frames 2–3 before sweeping left in frames 4–5 to face the nearby person, while the hooded figure at the back remains stationary ~2–2.5 m behind and to the right of the nearby person, with its lower body occluded by the clothing rack. Compared to the RGB strip alone, the depth map clearly separates the distance layers of the overlapping garments on the rack, the foreground hand versus the person's torso in frame 5, and the structural depth of the ceiling window frame in frame 3 despite dark lighting and glare. However, the map is unreliable on reflective and transparent glass surfaces (interpreting the red reflection/dome in frames 1–2 as a solid object at ~2.5 m and misestimating depth through the glass in frame 3) and degrades into a blurry, featureless gradient during the heavy motion blur of frame 4.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates foreground entities against a black background within the indoor room, identifying the person on the far left (~0.5–1 m away, within arm's reach), the dark hooded figure or mannequin near the back glass doors (~2.5–3 m away, ~2 m behind the foreground person), and vertical sections of the hanging garments on the right-center clothing rack (~1–2 m away, ~1 m to the right of the foreground person). In frame 1, the foreground person is partly out of view on the left edge, the hooded figure stands in the left-center background facing away toward the doors, a red circular dome behind the glass is segmented above the rack, and four hanging garment sections are segmented side by side below it; in frame 2, as the camera turns right, only the garments remain segmented while both people leave or blur out of detection. During the upward tilt and fast pan in frames 3 and 4, no instances are segmented at all, whereas in frame 5 the camera turns left to show the nearby person on the left (~0.8 m away, facing the camera wearer and looking slightly downward/left) and the distant hooded figure on the right (~2.5 m away, facing away and merged with the adjacent clothing rack which occludes its lower half). This map makes it easier than the blurry RGB frames to distinguish individual vertical garment bundles on the rack in frames 1–2 and cleanly separates the nearby person's silhouette from the background clutter in frames 1 and 5. However, the segmentation map is unreliable across much of the sequence: it misclassifies the hanging clothes as 'suitcase' and the red window reflection/dome as 'umbrella', completely misses all objects during the camera tilt and motion blur in frames 2–4, fails to separate the foreground arm from the person's torso in frame 5, and merges the background hooded figure with the foreground clothing rack in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks 2D body and hand skeletons in the room, detecting keypoints only in frames 1, 2, and 5 while remaining completely blank during the upward camera tilt in frame 3 and rapid turning blur in frame 4. In frame 1 (around the rack ~1.5–2 m away) and frame 2, small yellow torso polygons and head/face keypoint clusters are placed near the upper left of the clothing rack and the red dome reflection (~2–3 m away), without detecting the actual person partially visible at the far left edge (~0.5 m away) or the dark hooded figure by the doors (~2.5–3 m away). By frame 5, after the camera wearer turns left, a large yellow upper-body trapezoid and facial keypoints appear on the left for the nearby person (~0.8 m away, within arm's reach), showing their shoulders squared toward the camera wearer and their head angled slightly downward, while a dense cluster of magenta hand keypoints at the bottom center (~0.3–0.5 m away, within immediate reach of both the camera wearer and the person's chest) captures a raised hand in front of their lower torso. The pose map makes the exact articulation of the blurred foreground fingers and hand in frame 5 and the person's shoulder-and-head orientation much clearer than in the motion-blurred RGB image alone. However, it is highly unreliable in frames 1 and 2 where it hallucinates miniature body skeletons onto the clothing hangers and window reflection, completely misses the dark hooded figure in frames 1, 2, and 5, and conflates the foreground raised arm in frame 5 with the standing person's own left wrist and hip joints.
